subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: (1) [3:666] Where policy defines “claim”: If the policy contains a definition of “claim,” that definition controls. (a) [3:667] Typical definition: Many D&O policies contain a definition of claim that includes: “judicial or administrative proceedings or written demand against a director or officer for which such director or officer may be subjected to a binding adjudication of liability.” [3:668 - 3:669] Reserved. (b) [3:670] Coercive vs. conciliatory “administrative proceedings”: Whether an administrative proceeding before a state or federal agency constitutes a “claim” under such a policy depends on whether the administrative agency has coercive power (i.e., the power to impose “binding adjudication of liability”) or merely powers of conciliation. 1) [3:671] EEOC proceedings: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) has powers of conciliation only. The EEOC only investigates and seeks voluntary compliance. Thus, the filing of a charge with the EEOC does not constitute a “claim.” [See Bensalem Township v. Western World Ins. Co.
